translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Narration tôi; Sultana and Sara use em/chị; Ladyland’s collective we is exclusive chúng tôi and the narrator’s Indian women chúng em; the Queen uses ta and các khanh, and her officials thần.
decisions.rationale: Vietnamese pronouns sharpen the contrast between the two societies without added explanation.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: The arms (weapons/limbs) pun had become a non sequitur; now vũ lực / sức vóc keeps the exchange logical.
Rhetorical ‘Thank you!’ is ‘There you are!’: Đấy, thấy chưa!
The Lady Principal now addresses the Queen as thần, matching the court register.
sacred relations fixed as người thân thiêng liêng; first cousins no longer narrowed to paternal cousins.
untrained men restored as chưa được thuần hóa, echoing the wild-animal comparison; Purity personified in 1.129 as in 1.15.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: Kept as the culture-specific terms on which the satirical reversal depends.
One fixed term for the kin with whom secluded women may mix.
Vietnamese has no single word for weapons and limbs; force and physique keep the logical link of the exchange.

witness_decision: Selected the complete text in the University of Pennsylvania ‘A Celebration of Women Writers’ edition (ed. Mary Mark Ockerbloom), which records first publication in The Indian Ladies’ Magazine, Madras, 1905. A scan of the 1905 magazine issue or the 1908 Calcutta book edition could not be located on the assessment date, so this electronic text is not collated with a print facsimile; English Wikisource reproduces the same text.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The Queen uses exclusive chúng tôi when speaking for Ladyland to a foreign guest, after ta in court; kept as a national we.

title_review.rationale: Giấc mơ của Sultana is the literal title and matches giấc mơ in the body, including the ‘sentimental nightmare’ exchange.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Compared the dream frame, Sara, the reversed purdah dialogue and the arrival at Sara’s house.
Compared the household, the sun-heat and cloud inventions, the history of the war and the mardana.
Compared religion, sacred relations, the air-car, the Queen and the waking.
